name: Water From Your Eyes
label: Matador
lede: Rachel Brown and Nate Amos started out wanting to write New Order songs. By 2024 they were opening for Interpol in front of about 160,000 people, and in 2025 they landed a record in Pitchfork's top 20.

eras.title: Songs like New Order, from a Chicago house show
eras.text: Two people from the Chicago DIY circuit decide to write songs together, then move the whole operation to Brooklyn. The first records are small, weird and self-made.

years.src: Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes · Wikipedia: Nate Amos · Wikipedia: Rachel Brown (musician)
years.h: Rachel Brown meets Nate Amos at a Chicago house show
years.p: Brown was home from NYU for the summer; Amos was hosting a DIY show at his place. The pitch they made each other: write songs like New Order.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the meeting to 2015 and the band's formation to 2016. Brown had been recording alone as thanks for coming since high school, and Amos had been making records as [[This Is Lorelei|a2d140d8-ae17-4d72-b680-b89c77f1ed52]] since around 2013.

Brown's version of the origin, as Wikipedia relays it: "Nate showed me New Order, and we wanted to make New Order kinds of songs." Both later moved to Brooklyn.

years.h: Long Days, No Dreams comes out while Brown is still at NYU
years.p: Nothing on the 2017 album sounds like the band that came later, which is half the reason to go back.

years.src: Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes discography · Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes
years.h: All a Dance EP lands on Exploding in Sound
years.p: The Massachusetts label would also put out the follow-up, Somebody Else's Song. Guitarist and keyboardist Michael Kolb joined the live band the same year.
years.xp: Wikipedia's discography lists All a Dance as a January 19, 2018 EP on Exploding in Sound. Kolb stayed in the live band until 2022.

eras.title: Recording through the lockdown
eras.text: Brown and Amos keep recording through a pandemic and a breakup, and borrow a structure from Scott Walker. Critics start to notice.

years.h: Somebody Else's Song is the first record people write about
years.p: Reviews of the Exploding in Sound release picked out the storytelling, the dreamy melodies and Brown's bittersweet delivery.
Recorded and released by the band during the COVID-19 pandemic, and named for its running time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Structure · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Structure turns a breakup into two matching halves
years.p: Eight tracks modeled on Scott Walker's Climate of Hunter, with two versions of "Quotations". Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Structure was recorded in 2020 as the romantic relationship between Brown and Amos ended, and that its layout was modeled on Scott Walker's Climate of Hunter. Amos described it as two matching halves with alternating song types.

Pitchfork's Phillipe Roberts called it "cryptic indie pop that hits like a sugar rush"; Paste's Max Freedman gave it 7.8. Later, Brown told The Line of Best Fit the working dynamic got better after the split: "it's so much better because it's way more fun."

eras.title: The longest talking phase
eras.text: Matador courts them for most of a year and lets them keep every strange thing about the band. The label debut is the record that makes them known.

years.src: PAPER: Water From Your Eyes Talk · Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes
years.h: Seven months of talks with Matador end in a signature
years.p: Talks began in December 2021 and closed in July 2022, per Brown and Amos in PAPER. Other labels had asked them to tone the experimental side down.
years.xp:
Brown's summary of the courtship, to PAPER: "It's the longest talking phase I've ever experienced." Amos said he arrived with a list of ways to stop the label from changing the band, and never needed it; Matador approved the finished album without notes.

Guitarist and bassist Al Nardo, of [[fantasy of a broken heart|15b40dbf-d08b-49de-8c33-12815c011d7b]], also joined the live band in 2022 as Kolb left.

years.src: Wikipedia: Everyone's Crushed · The Line of Best Fit
years.p: Nine songs in 31 minutes: the Matador debut got an 8.3 and Best New Music from Pitchfork.
years.xp:
Metacritic scored it 84 from 14 reviews. Brown told The Line of Best Fit the album was about the American sprawl: strip malls and desolate suburbs standing in for how "Americans failed the American people."

The Guardian called it "the only recent album that sounds the way it does." Rolling Stone ranked it No. 36 and NME No. 28 for 2023.

years.src: PAPER: Water From Your Eyes Talk
years.h: "Barley" is picked for an iPhone ad
years.p: PAPER reported the single was chosen for an upcoming Apple iPhone commercial, on the strength of its looped, instantly recognizable sounds.
years.xp: Amos told PAPER he had not thought of "Barley" as a standalone single at all.

years.h: Amos cold-emails a black-metal artist for the remix album
years.p: Crushed by Everyone came out November 17, with remixes from The Dare and Kassie Krut. Amos also wrote to experimental black metal artist Jute Gyte, whom he had followed for years.

eras.title: Bigger rooms
eras.text: Drummer Bailey Wollowitz makes it a four-piece, and a booking in Mexico City puts them in front of the largest crowd of their lives.

years.src: PAPER: Water From Your Eyes Talk
years.h: Bailey Wollowitz joins on drums for the Squid tour
years.p: The duo becomes a four-piece for the run with UK post-punk band Squid. Wollowitz, like Al Nardo, plays in [[fantasy of a broken heart|15b40dbf-d08b-49de-8c33-12815c011d7b]].
years.xp: PAPER reported the February 2024 Squid dates as the point where Wollowitz joined permanently. Wikipedia lists him as a member since 2023.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Interpol in Mexico City · Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes
years.h: Opening for [[Interpol|b23e8a63-8f47-4882-b55b-df2c92ef400e]] in front of about 160,000 at the Zócalo
years.p: Wikipedia puts the crowd at about 160,000 for the free show in Mexico City, which Rolling Stone called Interpol's biggest ever.
years.xp: Mexican press including Infobae ran explainers on who the American opener was. Wikipedia describes it as the band's largest concert.

years.h: MP3 Player 1 fills the gap between the two big albums
years.p: A stopgap EP on Matador, out July 12, 2024.

eras.title: It's a Beautiful Place
eras.text: A quieter, heavier, more existential record earns a spot in Pitchfork's top 20.

years.h: "Life Signs" arrives with a video Brown directed
years.p: The lead single from It's a Beautiful Place traps the duo in an endless loop of TV shows and commercials.
years.xp: Amos told Nylon the song's guitar part began as a 24-note quarter-tone series generated by a random number generator, then was reworked toward regular rock. Amos produced with audio engineer Howie Weinberg. Rolling Stone's Jon Blistein described the video as the duo "trapped in an endless loop of television."

years.h: "Nights in Armor" goes out four days before the album
years.p: The third single, after "Life Signs" (June 4) and "Playing Classics" (July 15).

years.src: Wikipedia: It's a Beautiful Place · Album of the Year: It's A Beautiful Place · NME: It's A Beautiful Place review
years.h: Pitchfork puts It's a Beautiful Place at No. 17 for 2025
years.p: It first drew an 8.3 from Pitchfork; Metacritic averaged 82 from 15 critics.
years.xp:
Recorded across 2024 and 2025 mostly in Amos's bedroom and in New York, the ten-track, 29-minute record deals in cosmic insignificance and whether optimism is possible. NME described sci-fi sounds, "frightening existentialism" and a newfound heaviness.

Paste scored it 8.7; Clash, Exclaim! and PopMatters 8. Beyond Pitchfork, it landed at No. 19 on Stereogum's list and No. 55 on Rolling Stone's, and at No. 21 on the UK Independent Albums chart. Album of the Year lists its Pitchfork score as 83.

yt: Live at Village Underground, London, Nov 13, 2025
years.h: First headline tour covers North America, then Europe
years.p: The North American run went from September 22 to November 7, with European dates from November 13 to December 7.
A Matador follow-up to the album, out December 3, 2025.
